text:
maya: Heads-up — RFC follow-up: we need an escape-hatch pattern for the planned API deprecation (v2 -> v3). thinking a feature-flag on the router + opt-in header for SDKs.

sam: +1. can you sketch the flow? is this tenant-level or request-level?

maya: tenant-level flag gated in our feature-flag service, with a per-request header `X-RW-Compat: legacy` that clients/SDKs can set while they migrate. router checks flag for tenant, if flag ON then we allow legacy semantics even when v3 is default.

jordan: so default behavior is v3. flag=true -> treat as v2, flag=false -> strict v3. how do we avoid flag sprawl?

tessa: recommend short TTL on flags and strict telemetry to auto-expire. also add a global kill-switch (release-bot) for incidents.

maya: exactly. plan: 1) SDKs add header when `compat_mode` is enabled 2) Console exposes tenant opt-in 3) Router reads feature-flag+header precedence: header overrides tenant opt-in for debugging 4) telemetry emits `compat.used` with reason tag.

sam: what about third-party clients not using SDKs? they'd need a migration guide to set header or else they'll get v3. can we auto-inject for some legacy proxies?

jordan: auto-injecting at edges is risky. maybe provide a sidecar snippet for on-prem/dedicated customers to translate old shapes to new one while they move. sidecar can set header if it sees old `Authorization` style or old envelope.

maya: Good idea — sidecar for Dedicated/Private. Hosted customers should rely on SDKs/docs.

tessa: fallback behavior if header present but migration still fails? return `200` with `compat-warning` header or send `420`?

sam: prefer graceful warnings. return v3-normal responses but include `X-RW-Compat-Warn: migration-required;details=...` and increment a telemetry counter. Hard errors only if header absent and payload is incompatible.

jordan: how about rollout strategy? feature-flag per tenant + canary internal tenants first, then beta customers, then all. each stage 24h min with health checks: error rate, latency, mismatch rate (how often we had to fallback).

maya: rollout checklist draft:
- implement header support in SDKs (js, py, go)
- router: flag check + header precedence + logging
- console: tenant opt-in UI + bulk opt-in API
- sidecar: template + docs for dedicated/on-prem
- metrics: `compat.used`, `compat.warn`, `compat.error`, `compat.sidecar-injected`
- expire automation: `flag.age > 90d -> alert owner`

tessa: add `prompt_on_use` event so customer-success can proactively contact tenants still using compat after N days.

sam: curious about performance impact — router will check feature-flag at request time. cache flag decisions for 10s? 60s?

jordan: cache per-tenant flag in router with TTL 30s and a streaming invalidation channel for immediate revokes. we already have that infra for AB tests.

maya: security/abuse: header could be forged if someone spoofs tenant id. router must validate header only when client cert/SDK token matches or when tenant-level opt-in allows header overrides. header override allowed only from trusted SDKs (by signing) or from sidecar IP ranges.

sam: how do SDKs sign header? HMAC with API key? we already send API key in Auth; maybe allow only tokens minted by SDK that include `sdk=true` claim. Router verifies token.

tessa: ops: add a `compat-escape` audit log entry for every request where compat used. retention 30d. tie to SLOs.

jordan: testing: add unit/integ tests for precedence matrix: tenant-flag=T, header=F -> legacy; tenant-flag=F, header=T -> legacy (if allowed); tenant-flag=F, header=T but token not sdk -> reject header.

maya: can someone own the RFC follow-up and implementation tracker? I can own router + metrics. Sam take SDK changes. Jordan sidecar + tests. Tessa deploy + console + CS hooks.

sam: I’ll open SDK PRs with opt-in flag and header support; will add automated telemetry emission.

jordan: will prototype sidecar Lua snippet for nginx + basic tests.

tessa: I’ll add console UI mock and update rollout doc.

release-bot: deployment reminder: canary build available at `ci/builds/1755-compat-escape-1` :rocket:

maya: great. next check-in Friday 11am. tagging @product for migration comms. :thumbsup:
